notes: PARTIAL table: only glyphs with direct visual-alignment evidence are 'certain'. Several high-frequency Catherine glyphs (p, g, z, a, o, x, E, f) could NOT be mapped with confidence and are listed under 'uncertain' or omitted. Glyph names are visual ASCII approximations. 'Y' (Catherine's xi-like glyph) is assumed identical to Charles IX 'xi' by shape description; verify against plate if test is promising. The '≠1'->'QUE' nomenclator shows multi-glyph codes exist; single '≠' (Catherine '!') may differ.
source: George Lasry's 2022 interlinear decipherment of the Charles IX -> Philibert du Croc cipher (Destray 1924, p.80; same book/period/correspondent as the Catherine cipher). Images: data/lasry-charlesIX-decipher-recto.png (sha256 747ae99d...) and data/lasry-charlesIX-decipher-verso.png (sha256 aa2f5445...), via cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/GL/. Transcribed 2026-10-07 by column-alignment of black cipher glyphs against red plaintext letters. Pairing direction: red ABOVE <-> black BELOW (proven by '≠1'->'QUE' nomenclator anchor, verso row 0).
